name: Model UN Week
description: An event introducing how Model UN builds global awareness, civic engagement, and communication skills through simulation-based learning.

name: Women Build Sponsored Habitat for Humanity
description: A hands-on build and fundraising initiative that supports affordable housing while creating a supportive space for women volunteers and advocates.

name: Invasive Plant Removal at Wrightwood Park
description: A local environmental restoration event focused on removing invasive species and helping improve habitat health at Wrightwood Park.

name: Teen Science Cafe
description: An informal evening event for teens featuring conversations with STEM professionals, hands-on activities, and a relaxed environment designed to spark curiosity and exploration.

name: Future Teacher Conference at UNCW
description: The Future Teacher Conference invites high school, community college, and homeschool students to UNCW for a day exploring life as a Watson student. Participants attend interactive sessions led by faculty and staff, along with a student panel focused on education careers.

name: Engineering Open House at NC State
description: The annual College of Engineering Open House at NC State offers prospective students and families an opportunity to explore engineering programs and learn more about the college.

name: Jambalaya Soul Slam
description: A spoken word and poetry event celebrating creative writing, performance, and storytelling.

name: Jambalaya Soul Slam Academy Writing & Performance Workshop
description: The Jambalaya Soul Academy provides poetry workshops that offer writing strategies, prompts, and opportunities to develop and share poems with other writers.

name: Morehead Observatory Guest Night
description: The Department of Physics and Astronomy hosts a weekly public astronomy program at the Morehead Observatory, featuring a short presentation, observatory tour, and telescope viewing when weather permits.

name: JA Inspire Career Expo
description: Junior Achievement of Eastern NC offers early career-focused programs to help students explore future pathways before high school. JA Inspire extends learning beyond the classroom by connecting students to career opportunities and planning for high school, college, and beyond.

name: JA Stock Market Challenge
description: Teams of 3–4 students use $500,000 in mock stock to trade fictitious companies during a fast-paced, 60-day simulated market. The objective is to earn the highest return, with top teams qualifying for the Junior Achievement national competition.

name: UNC Science Expo
description: The UNC Science Expo, hosted by Morehead Planetarium and Science Center, is a large annual science festival featuring hands-on activities, demonstrations, and exhibits led by UNC-Chapel Hill students, faculty, and community partners.

name: Durham Arts Council - The Art of the Party
description: The Art of the Party is a lively celebration of Durham’s creative spirit, bringing together music, food, culture, and community while supporting the arts through an immersive event and live auction.

name: Carolina Jazz Festival
description: Enjoy live jazz performances by touring bands, artists in residence, and UNC Department of Music faculty and students at this annual February festival celebrating jazz.

name: Nevermore Film Festival
description: Founded in 1999, this juried festival showcases horror, science fiction, mystery, thriller, animated, and dark fantasy films from around the world at the Carolina Theatre. With over 1,000 films screened, it is internationally recognized as a leading genre film festival.

name: Art in Bloom at the North Carolina Museum of Art
description: This art and flower festival at the North Carolina Museum of Art highlights regional floral designers who create arrangements inspired by the museum’s artwork. Proceeds from the event support the NCMA Foundation.

name: GRAHAM100: The Centennial Celebration
description: The Martha Graham Dance Company returns to Carolina Performing Arts for its 12th appearance with GRAHAM100: The Centennial Celebration. The program marks the culmination of the company’s three-season 100th anniversary celebration and explores the question, “What is an American?”

name: Eclipse
description: Culture Mill returns with a remount of Eclipse, a Carolina Performing Arts–commissioned work that invites audiences and artists to imagine collective monument building. Held outdoors at CURRENT ArtSpace, the performance uses movement and restorative justice practices to explore how shared bodies and stories can create new forms of togetherness.

name: Jazz at Lincoln Center Orchestra with Wynton Marsalis
description: The Jazz at Lincoln Center Orchestra with Wynton Marsalis returns to Carolina Performing Arts, delivering a vibrant performance that blends swing, soul, and storytelling through their signature sound and dynamic chemistry.

name: Mahler Chamber Orchestra
description: The Mahler Chamber Orchestra returns to Memorial Hall for its fourth Carolina Performing Arts appearance, presenting an evening of music by Prokofiev and Hindemith. The performance is led by GRAMMY Award–winning pianist Yuja Wang, who directs from the piano and is celebrated for her expressive artistry.

name: Shakori Hills Grassroots
description: Shakori Hills GrassRoots is a biannual, family-friendly festival in Pittsboro, North Carolina that celebrates music, dance, art, and education. Organized by the nonprofit Shakori Hills Community Arts Center, the festival features diverse musical acts, workshops, kids’ activities, crafts, and camping.

name: Triangle Trails Summit
description: The Triangle Trails Summit brings regional leaders, planners, and advocates together at Dix Chapel for a day focused on the future of the Triangle’s greenways and blueways. Through keynotes, discussions, and networking, the annual event explores ways to strengthen connectivity, accessibility, and sustainability across the region’s trail network.

name: Snow White - Carolina Ballet
description: This production brings the classic fairytale Snow White to life while exploring timeless themes of self-reflection and comparison. Choreographed by Artistic Director and CEO Zalman Raffael, with an original score by Shinji Eshima, the performance offers a thoughtful and modern interpretation of the beloved story.

name: North Carolina Symphony Beethoven Emperor Concerto
description: Beethoven’s bold and innovative “Emperor” Piano Concerto will be brought to life by guest soloist Anne-Marie McDermott, alongside Bartók’s vibrant Concerto for Orchestra, with Music Director Carlos Miguel Prieto leading the performance.

name: Appalachian Spring with the North Carolina Symphony
description: Music Director Carlos Miguel Prieto leads a program featuring Copland’s iconic Appalachian Spring, along with Gabriela Ortiz’s Kauyumari and Revueltas’s La Noche de los Mayas.

name: Beauty and the Beast - Carolina Ballet
description: Artistic Director Zalman Raffael unveils a world premiere, Beauty and the Beast, reimagining the timeless tale with fresh creativity and heart. Presented as a new full-length ballet with live music, the production draws audiences into a vividly realized world.

name: Shakespeare in the Park
description: Catch As You Like It at the Knightdale Station Park amphitheater. This abridged performance follows Rosalind, banished from court and in disguise, as she navigates mistaken identities, humor, and romance in the Forest of Arden. With witty banter and Shakespeare’s beautiful poetry, it’s a light, enjoyable way to experience the play outdoors or on a busy schedule.

name: Chapel Hill Events Guide
description: Enjoy great food, live music, and more. Discover a rich arts and history scene through museums, historic homes, murals, and live performances. Take in the area’s natural beauty along greenways, trails, preserves, and riverwalks. Browse shops for one-of-a-kind finds like vintage treasures, locally made pottery, or classic Tar Heel souvenirs.

name: Discover Durham - Events Guide
description: Every day in the Bull City, there’s something happening. With thousands of Durham-based events each year, you’ll find concerts, festivals, fundraisers, art shows, and community gatherings for all ages and interests—perfect for locals and visitors alike.

name: Bull City Madness
description: Bull City Madness returns on Saturday, April 25, 2026, bringing Durham’s 3v3 basketball tournament back to celebrate the city’s deep basketball legacy. The event unites the community through friendly competition while raising awareness and support for local organizations doing meaningful work in Durham.

name: SMathHacks 2026
description: SMathHacks is NCSSM’s annual 36-hour hackathon open to students across NC, where participants collaborate to create innovative software and connect with peers.

name: Durham Earth Day Festival
description: Join us in celebrating Earth Day 2026 as we come together to honor and protect our planet. This year’s theme, “Our Power, Our Planet,” emphasizes the ability of individuals, communities, businesses, and governments to take meaningful action and work collectively toward a more sustainable future.

name: Canine Field Day
description: Enjoy a day in the park with your furry friend at Canine Field Day! Bring your dog to participate in a variety of fun activities for all energy levels, including an agility course, non-competitive Frisbee and fetch areas, bobbing for treats, a treasure hunt, and more. After your pup has burned off some energy, take a stroll through the pet market or grab a bite to eat from the food trucks. 🐶🌳

name: Bimbé Cultural Arts Festival
description: The nationally award-winning Bimbé Cultural Arts Festival will celebrate its 56th anniversary on May 16, 2026! Join us for a vibrant day featuring live music, arts and crafts, community resources, traditional food, and performances from talented local artists. Stay tuned for upcoming announcements about headlining acts and performers. 🎶🎨

name: July 4th Celebration
description: Celebrate community pride with Durham Parks and Recreation and the Durham Bulls. Attend the baseball game and enjoy an exciting fireworks show following the game.

name: Durham Fiesta Latina
description: Save the date for Durham Fiesta Latina, presented by Durham Parks & Recreation in partnership with El Centro Hispano. This annual event celebrates Latino culture with authentic food, live music, folkloric dancing, family activities, and community resources.

name: Barktoberfest
description: Durham Parks and Recreation and Beyond Fences host Barktoberfest, a fun-filled celebration for dogs and their humans that brings the community together for a day of canine activities, festive entertainment, and tasty treats.

name: Santa Monica Teen Center
description: The St. Monica Teen Center is the perfect place for teens to hang out and explore a variety of activities. Whether you’re into cooking, sports, video games, or movie nights, there’s something for everyone to enjoy. Best of all, access is free with a Raleigh Teen Connect Membership.

name: Dix Park Outdoor Yoga
description: Middle and high school students are invited to relax and unwind at Dix Park with outdoor yoga sessions. Open to all fitness levels, this experience encourages connection with nature while promoting wellness. Be sure to bring a yoga mat, a towel, and a filled water bottle.

name: Dix Park Trace 'n Paint Crafternoon
description: Learn how to use graphite paper to transfer a printed image onto a canvas panel, then bring it to life with acrylic paint. Choose from Creative Camps’ detailed designs or create your own unique piece.

name: Music at the Market
description: Join us on the patio for great music spun by the talented DJs of Oak City Soul Vinyl Collective while enjoying a perfect picnic in the park. House of Many Porches will be offering a variety of snacks, sandwiches, coffee, baked goods, wine, and beer to complete the experience.

name: Dix Park Guided Walking Tour
description: Lace up your walking shoes and join us for a 2.5-mile tour of Dix Park, where you’ll explore the site’s history, discover what the City’s largest urban park offers today, and learn about its transformation from a former state hospital campus into a world-class destination.

name: Dix Park Breathwork
description: Join us for an afternoon of guided breathwork and meditation designed to help you relax, release tension, and boost your mood and energy.

name: Raleigh Parks from Bond to Beyond
description: Join Raleigh Parks for a fun, family-friendly afternoon to learn about the progress of 23 Parks Bond projects across the city, meet the people behind the work, and see how community support turns into parks that benefit everyone.

name: Instrument Petting Zoo
description: Join us for an interactive music experience for all ages, featuring a hands-on “instrument petting zoo” where you can explore, try instruments, and make music together—no experience needed. Enjoy performances by youth quartets, play along with easy instruments, and take part in a creative art activity painting old instruments with the Raleigh Music Collective.

name: Forest Bathing
description: In Japan, forest walks known as shinrin-yoku, or “forest bathing,” are an important part of preventative health care. Join us for a guided talk and walk exploring the history, research, and health benefits of forest bathing while experiencing it firsthand around Dix Park’s Stone Houses, Grove, and Greenway—be prepared for hills and uneven terrain, and wear closed-toe shoes.

name: Bird Watching
description: Learn about the resident and migratory birds of Dix Park while building your bird identification skills through sight and sound. Discover tips for recognizing sparrows, woodpeckers, hawks, and more, and contribute to real scientific data by helping track how bird diversity changes in the park over time.

name: A Burden Too Great to Bear: PTSD and the Civil War
description: The Civil War brought about a major mental health crisis in the United States, affecting both soldiers and civilians with lasting impacts that led many to institutions like Dorothea Dix Hospital. Historian Ernest Dollar examines the causes of post traumatic stress disorder and the role of the state’s first asylum during the war.

name: Tai Chi
description: Tai Chi is a practice of slow, continuous movements that flow in all directions to promote balance and well-being. It has been shown to reduce stress and anxiety, improve mental and physical balance, and support overall health. This program is open to all fitness levels and youth ages 12 and up, and minors must be registered and accompanied by an adult.

name: Poetry in the Park
description: Join us for a relaxed open mic gathering in the park celebrating poetry, short stories, and works in progress. Whether you are an experienced writer, a first time reader, or just want to listen, everyone is welcome to enjoy an evening of creativity and community.

name: Raleigh Earth Day
description: Join the City of Raleigh for the 5th annual Raleigh Earth Day, a milestone event that brings together community members, local organizations, and city departments for an evening focused on environmental stewardship, sustainability, and connection in one of Raleigh’s most beautiful public spaces.

name: Public Library Pop-Up
description: Join Wake County Public Libraries for a family friendly pop up where you can sign up for a library card, check out items, and return borrowed materials. Enjoy family story time with interactive books, music, rhymes, and movement designed to build early reading skills for young children.

name: Teen Vendor Market
description: Shop from over two dozen teen makers, artists, and entrepreneurs as they showcase their creative work at this fun outdoor vendor market in Gipson Play Plaza.

name: Guided Trolley Tour
description: Hop on the Raleigh Trolley for a 2 hour tour to explore the history of Dix Park, discover what the city’s largest urban park offers today, and learn about its transformation from a former hospital campus into a world class destination.

name: Inter-Tribal Pow Wow
description: Presented in partnership with Triangle Native American Society, enjoy a day of competition dancing and drumming, vendors, and music that celebrate the rich legacy and culture of Indigenous communities in North Carolina at the annual Dix Park Inter Tribal Pow Wow.

name: Capital City Juneteenth Celebration
description: The community is invited to gather for an afternoon of reflection and celebration in honor of Juneteenth, the oldest nationally recognized commemoration of the end of slavery in the United States.

name: Summer Solstice Sunrise Yoga
description: Yoga is a practice of connection that brings us closer to ourselves and to one another. Join us for an open level, vinyasa based session that encourages reflection, personal expression, and a sense of community. This special gathering celebrates the summer solstice with themes of light, renewal, and intentional presence as we welcome the longest day of the year. Please arrive at 5:45 am to find a spot, and we will begin shortly after 6:00 am.

name: Kirby Derby
description: Enjoy an annual celebration filled with costumes, creativity, and plenty of silliness. The event features an offbeat parade, a kids pinebox car competition, and an exciting soapbox derby.

name: Trophy Trot 5k
description: Kick off your Thanksgiving Day in Raleigh’s premier park with a morning 5K race at Dix Park, all in support of Healing Transitions, followed by an afterparty at Trophy Brewing.

name: The 25-year Handmade Book Project | Emily Eve Weinstein Exhibit
description: This solo exhibition features 17 hand bound volumes that document the artist’s work year by year, each accompanied by autobiographical essays. Begun in 2009, the ongoing project traces a creative life through painting, writing, and experimental bookmaking, with many of the featured oil paintings also on display.

name: The Whimsical Naturalist: NC Flora & Fauna | Katie Crawford Allen
description: In The Whimsical Naturalist, North Carolina artist Katie Crawford Allen highlights the rich biodiversity of the East Coast and the connections between species, ecosystems, and communities. Through watercolor portraits of native plants and animals, she uses anthropomorphism to encourage viewers to reflect on their relationship with the environment and one another.

name: Color Concentrated: A Salon-Style Show from the Robertson Collection
description: Color Concentrated offers a bold contrast to last year’s Color Triumphant by bringing the same modern artworks together on a single, densely arranged wall of color rather than presenting them in a spacious, chronological layout. Inspired by the layered look of museum storage racks, the Robertsons’ home displays, and nineteenth century Parisian Salon exhibitions, the installation emphasizes the expressive power of color in a striking new way.

name: Artful Watercolors | Beginner's Watercolor Workshop
description: Join us for a hands on watercolor workshop with Abhi where you will explore the basics of painting, including color mixing, brush techniques, and composition, in a fun and engaging environment.

name: Soft Night, Watching | Jen Clay Interactive Gallery Exhibit
description: This fall, the Ackland Art Museum at the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill presents Soft Night, Watching, an immersive fabric installation by artist Jen Clay that invites visitors into a vivid world of texture, imagination, and quilted monsters. The interactive exhibition offers a multisensory exploration of fear, neurodivergence, and the unexpected comfort found in the unknown.

name: Annual 1843 Pleyel Piano Concert
description: The Department of Music presents its annual concert featuring the historic 1843 Pleyel piano.

name: UNC Music Research Forum | Spring 2026
description: The UNC Music Research Forum features invited lectures by distinguished scholars from around the world along with informal research presentations from department members and campus colleagues. Held on the final Friday of each month during the semester from 3:30 to 5:00 pm in Person Recital Hall, it serves as an intellectual hub and is open to all.

name: Collage Workshop with Theresa P-Tan
description: Explore collage as an accessible and low pressure creative practice in this free workshop led by Theresa P Tan. Participants will learn collage techniques through guided prompts and open work time.

name: Intro to Sashiko Stitching | Japanese Embroidery Workshop
description: Sashiko, meaning small stitches or piercing, is a traditional Japanese embroidery technique used to both decorate and strengthen textiles. Originating from the 18th century practice of boro developed by farmers and the working class, it has recently gained popularity in the West. In this workshop, participants will explore the cultural context of sashiko, including the difference between appreciation and appropriation, while learning this meditative technique from Japanese American artist River Takada, who grew up between Carrboro and Tokyo.

name: Ink & Flow | Black Ink Drawing Workshop | Ages 15+
description: Ink drawing is a centuries old technique that began in Asia and later spread around the world, known for its immediacy and expressive line work. In this workshop, participants will explore foundational exercises and create observational pieces using a variety of ink techniques, embracing the fluid and unpredictable nature of the medium. Open to ages 15 and up, the class welcomes both beginners and experienced artists interested in experimenting with new forms of expression.

name: DIYLeaf Monthly Craft Club | Paper Flowers
description: Come craft with us each month as we guide you through a new project with all supplies provided. No experience is needed and everyone is welcome.

name: Timo Andres, pianist | Guest Artist Recital Masterclass
description: Timo Andres is a composer and pianist from rural Connecticut who now lives in Brooklyn, New York. His recent work includes a solo recital debut at Carnegie Hall and the premiere of a piano concerto for Aaron Diehl with the Los Angeles Philharmonic conducted by John Adams. He also created orchestrations for Justin Peck’s production of Illinoise, which had acclaimed runs in multiple cities and on Broadway, earning him a 2024 Tony Award nomination for Best Orchestrations.

name: Flute Studio Spring Recital
description: A performance featuring the flute students of Dr. Kelariz Keshavarz.

name: Starry Nights: Spring Skies
description: Find your next date night or spring celebration at Morehead Planetarium and Science Center with the Starry Nights series, an engaging live program for adults and older teens that offers an in depth tour of the Chapel Hill night sky.

name: Chance Encounter | Heather Hayman Gallery Exhibit
description: After three decades as a graphic designer in the publishing and music industries, Heather Hayman now focuses on found still life photography, a practice she began in 2003. Her first solo exhibition, Chance Encounter, features recent work from Spain, Japan, Aruba, and North Carolina, with additional images published in zines through her imprint, Triple Digit Press.

name: Rough Draft | Poetry Workshop
description: Join us for a monthly poetry workshop led by Donovan Livingston, the Poet Laureate of Chapel Hill.

name: My Muses Sketchbook Circle
description: Begin your month in a calm, creative setting with Sketchbook Mornings, a free and welcoming gathering for anyone who enjoys slowing down and observing the world. Whether you are an experienced artist or simply curious, all are invited to connect, reflect, and create.

name: Clarinet Studio Spring Recital
description: Clarinet students of Donald Oehler and David Allen

name: UNC Hip-Hop Ensemble Spring Concert
description: A performance by the UNC Hip-Hop Ensemble, directed by Kerwin Young.

name: James & Susan Moeser Auditorium in Hill Hall
description: Hosts a variety of concerts and lectures, many of which are free and open to the public.

name: 'The Price' by Arthur Miller | RedBird Theatre Company
description: Family dynamics, the meaning of material possessions, and the weight of personal choices come together in a powerful story about confronting the past and finding hope for the future.

name: Carolina Vibe Dance Team Spring Showcase
description: Carolina Vibe is a student run, student choreographed dance team rooted in creativity, collaboration, and community. Each piece in this year’s show is created by its members, giving dancers the opportunity to lead, choreograph, and bring their own artistic visions to life.

name: Tarheel Antique Festival
description: Join us for a day or the entire weekend to enjoy the love of antiques through our vendors booths, appraisals and onsite auction over this weekend event Friday through Sunday.

name: 2nd Friday ArtWalk | Extended Museum Hours
description: Stroll through our galleries featuring highlights from a collection of over 21,000 works of art, browse the Museum Store, and sketch in the galleries using art supplies from our lobby’s art cart.

name: ChapBoro Book Crawl!
description: Grab a punch card at any participating location and collect punches as you go! (You can earn one punch per location, not per purchase.) Each punch you get also enters you into a raffle for exciting prizes from the participating spots.

name: Drawing in the Galleries
description: Join us this month for our popular Drawing in the Galleries program during Studio Saturday! Led by Amanda Hughes, this session invites participants to creatively explore a selected object from the Ackland’s collection. Using their own gallery-safe materials—such as paper or notebooks and dry media like pencils or crayons—everyone draws the same object and then comes together to share observations and insights.

name: Paint & Play with Baby Kangaroos
description: We’re offering a special one-time class featuring joeys! Join us for a family-friendly paint day where you’ll be greeted by two joeys. They’ll mingle with you during the class, and there will be time at the end for photos and snuggling. Please note that everyone in the studio must have a paid seat.

name: UNC Opera | MFE 25-26
description: UNC Opera, directed by Jeanne Fischer.

name: UNC Science Expo 2026 | North Carolina Science Festival
description: The UNC Science Expo is a signature event of the annual North Carolina Science Festival and one of the state’s largest celebrations of science. With over 100 booths hosted by UNC-Chapel Hill students, researchers, professionals, and community volunteers, the quads around Morehead Planetarium and Science Center come alive with activity. From hands-on games and demonstrations to behind-the-scenes lab tours, the Expo offers a fun and engaging way for people of all ages to explore science.

name: Art Adventures! | Morning & Afternoon Sessions
description: In this hands-on, art-inspired class for six- to nine-year-olds, participants will create their own artwork inspired by pieces on view. Space is limited, and registration is required.

name: Basket Weaving | Workshop
description: In this 4-hour workshop, learn to weave a beautiful and durable reed basket with a leather strap designed to fit your water bottle, helping you stay hydrated and stylish all summer long!

name: Brass Chamber Music Concert
description: Brass Chamber Music Ensembles, directed by Michael Kris.

name: UNC Guitar Ensemlble
description: UNC Guitar Ensemble, directed by Billy Stewart.

name: Mini Med School Lecture Series | Health Policy & the Healthcare System
description: Ever wondered how doctors think about diseases, treatments, and cutting-edge research? Mini Med School, hosted by the UNC MD-PhD program, offers a closer look. This program gives the local community insight into how physicians approach diseases and other medically focused topics.

name: The Rhythmic Forum | Carolina Center for Neurostimulation
University Band Spring Concert
description: Explore what happens in the brain when music comes alive at this engaging lunchtime experience where neuroscience meets live performance. Watch real-time brainwaves projected on screen during live music, try hands-on demonstrations, and join conversations with musicians and neuroscientists working in this emerging field. Presented by the Carolina Center for Neurostimulation, the event brings together art, research, and community to show how rhythm and sound shape the mind. Stay afterward to connect with performers and fellow attendees through conversation and reflection.

name: A Closer Look At One Work of Art | Ackland TOUR
description: Take a close, careful look at a single work of art from the Ackland collection with Andrea Bolland, Associate Professor Emerita of Art History at the University of Nebraska–Lincoln.

name: UNC Gamelan Nyai Saraswati Spring Concert
!Music Madness! | March Madness meets Classical Music
description: UpClose Chamber Music returns this April with a special event, Music Madness, on Thursday, April 16 at CURRENT Studio in Chapel Hill. Join the Chamber Orchestra of the Triangle for a unique experience where classical compositions meet the energy of college basketball. Eight new works by collegiate composers will be performed by the Durham Fellows String Quartet, and the audience will help decide who advances in this bracket-style competition. Cast your vote and help crown the winner!

name: SilverArts: Heritage & Visual Art Show
description: SilverArts is a celebration of creative expression and a key part of the Orange County and North Carolina Senior Games.

name: UNC Clef Hangers 2026 Spring Concert
description: The UNC Clef Hangers return to Memorial Hall on Thursday, April 16 for their Annual Spring Concert. Join UNC–Chapel Hill’s premier all-male a cappella group for an evening of harmony, humor, and high-energy performance. The concert features a wide-ranging repertoire, from classic hits to contemporary chart-toppers, all delivered with the Clef Hangers’ signature vocal arrangements and dynamic stage presence. A beloved campus tradition, this event brings the Carolina community together to celebrate student talent and live music.

name: UNC Jazz Combos 4, 5, 6
description: UNC Jazz Combos, coached by Dan Davis and Jason Foureman.
